import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 769

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/769](https://www.erdosproblems.com/769)
-/

namespace Erdos769

open Filter

open scoped Topology

/-- An axis-parallel homothetic copy of the standard `n`-cube. -/
structure Cube (n : ℕ) where
  lower : Fin n → ℝ
  side : ℝ

/-- Membership in the half-open cube `∏ j, [lower j, lower j + side)`. -/
def Cube.Mem {n : ℕ} (Q : Cube n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, Q.lower j ≤ x j ∧ x j < Q.lower j + Q.side

/-- Membership in the half-open unit cube `[0,1)^n`. -/
def InUnit {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 ≤ x j ∧ x j < 1

/-- A cube is nondegenerate and contained in the closed unit cube. -/
def Cube.InsideUnit {n : ℕ} (Q : Cube n) : Prop :=
  0 < Q.side ∧ ∀ j, 0 ≤ Q.lower j ∧ Q.lower j + Q.side ≤ 1

/-- `tiles` is an exact decomposition of the unit `n`-cube into `k` homothetic
cubes: every tile is a positive homothet inside the unit cube, and every point
of `[0,1)^n` belongs to exactly one half-open tile. -/
def IsTiling {n k : ℕ} (tiles : Fin k → Cube n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (tiles i).InsideUnit) ∧ ∀ x, InUnit x → ∃! i, (tiles i).Mem x

/-- Exactly `k` homothetic `n`-cubes can tile the unit `n`-cube. -/
def Admissible (n k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ tiles : Fin k → Cube n, IsTiling tiles

/-- `c` is the minimal cutoff `c(n)`: every `k ≥ c` is admissible, and (when
`c > 0`) `c - 1` is not. -/
def IsCutoff (n c : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ k, c ≤ k → Admissible n k) ∧ (c = 0 ∨ ¬Admissible n (c - 1))

/-- The highlighted conjecture `c(n) ≫ n^n`: there is an absolute positive
constant `A/B` with `c(n) ≥ (A/B) n^n` for all sufficiently large `n`. -/
def Erdos769LowerBound : Prop :=
  ∃ A B N : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ 0 < B ∧
    ∀ n c : ℕ, N ≤ n → IsCutoff n c → A * n ^ n ≤ B * c

/--
Let $c(n)$ be minimal such that if $k\geq c(n)$ then the $n$-dimensional unit
cube can be decomposed into $k$ homothetic $n$-dimensional cubes. Give good
bounds for $c(n)$ — in particular, is it true that $c(n)\gg n^n$?

The `c(n) \gg n^n` conjecture is **false**: for odd `n`, one can tile the unit
`n`-cube into `k` homothetic cubes for every `k ≥ U(n)` with `U(n)/n^n → 0`, so
`c(n)/n^n → 0` along odd dimensions and no absolute constant lower-bounds it.

Determining good bounds for `c(n)` in general remains open.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-769/Research/Solution.lean"]
theorem erdos_769 : answer(False) ↔ Erdos769LowerBound := by
  sorry

/--
What refuting $c(n)\gg n^n$ leaves open: give good bounds for $c(n)$. Asked here on the
scale the problem itself sets, $n^n$: does $c$ have a well-defined order
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c(n)}{n\log n}?$$
The refuted conjecture would have forced this limit to be at least $1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_769.variants.growth_rate :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, IsCutoff n (c n)) ∧
        ∃ γ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (c n) / (n * Real.log n)) atTop (𝓝 γ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos769

findings.description: The conjunct `(∀ n, IsCutoff n (c n))` on line 93 includes dimension zero and is impossible. The space `Fin 0 → ℝ` is a singleton, and both `InUnit x` and every `Q.Mem x` hold vacuously there. Consequently, `Admissible 0 k ↔ k = 1`. For any proposed cutoff c, its tail condition would require `Admissible 0 (c + 2)`, a contradiction. Thus the entire right-hand side is false independently of the logarithmic growth question. In `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, I proved `zero_dim_admissible_iff`, `zero_dim_no_cutoff`, and `growth_rate_rhs_false`; their axiom lists contain only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/769 asks: “Let c(n) be minimal such that if k ≥ c(n) then the n-dimensional unit cube can be decomposed into k homothetic n-dimensional cubes. Give good bounds for c(n).” It records c(2)=6 and the Burgess–Erdős bound c(n) ≪ n^(n+1). Erdős, “Remarks on some problems in number theory” (1974), §II, p. 199, likewise studies these finite cutoffs and their bounds. An asymptotic question about these cutoffs must not additionally demand a cutoff in dimension zero, where no such cutoff exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the cutoff condition to positive dimensions, for example `∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < n → IsCutoff n (c n)) ∧ ∃ γ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (c n) / (n * Real.log n)) atTop (𝓝 γ)`. Alternatively require `IsCutoff n (c n)` only eventually. Leave c(0) arbitrary; the quotient’s totalized values at n=0 and n=1 do not affect an atTop limit.

reformulations.difference: Uses unique coverage by half-open axis-parallel cubes instead of a decomposition of the closed cube into closed homothetic cubes with disjoint interiors.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite family of positive-sided cubes, unique half-open coverage implies closed coverage by taking closures: closure commutes with finite unions, and each half-open cube has the intended closed cube as its closure. Tile interiors are subsets of their half-open versions, so they are disjoint. Conversely, given a closed tiling with disjoint interiors, perturb any point of [0,1)^n slightly in every positive coordinate direction, choosing the perturbation small enough to avoid all finitely many coordinate boundary levels. A tile containing the perturbed point has the original point in its half-open version. If two half-open tiles contained that original point, a sufficiently small positive perturbation would lie in both interiors, a contradiction. This does not require the tiling to be face-to-face.

reformulations.difference: Expresses minimality using inadmissibility of c−1, with a separate c=0 case, rather than explicitly taking the least eventual-admissibility threshold.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Once every k≥c is admissible, failure of admissibility at c−1 rules out every smaller threshold. Conversely, if c is least and positive, admissibility of c−1 would make c−1 another threshold. The c=0 case is automatically least if its tail condition holds. I proved the exact equivalence with `IsLeast {d : ℕ | ∀ k, d ≤ k → Admissible n k} c` in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Uses positive natural numbers A,B and a cross-multiplied inequality, and quantifies over the relational predicate IsCutoff, instead of using a cutoff function and a positive real constant in the Vinogradov lower bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Cutoffs exist in every positive dimension and are unique. I verified existence using regular-grid refinements and coprime tile-count increments, and proved uniqueness from minimality. Any positive real lower-bound constant can be replaced by a smaller positive rational 1/(b+1); conversely A/B is a positive real constant, and multiplication by positive B preserves the inequality. Dimension zero is harmless here because the existential starting point N can be increased to at least 1. In positive-dim.lean I proved a full ↔ between Erdos769LowerBound and the existence of a positive-dimensional cutoff function with an eventual real-constant lower bound.

review.notes: The cited external proof was reconstructed in /workspace/review/external-proof.lean using the target file’s identical definitions. It compiled, and `#print axioms Erdos769.erdos769_lower_bound_false` returned only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Thus the main theorem’s negative answer and formal_proof record check out. The website’s overall OPEN label concerns the broader bounds problem; its proof-claims page explicitly records the odd-dimensional disproof of the uniform lower bound, so I do not report a status mismatch. The logarithmic-limit question is an explicitly introduced related variant, not a question stated verbatim in the cited source or an equivalent replacement for its entire request for good bounds. Boundary tests, cutoff equivalences, and positive-dimensional existence proofs are saved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and positive-dim.lean. The target file was not modified.
